title: Third contravariant Hom-colimit comparison for distinguished triangles
statement: Let J be a cofiltered category and D a pretriangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let H : J -> Triangle(D) be a functor all of whose values are distinguished, let U be a distinguished triangle, let j0 be an object of J, and let m : H(j0) -> U be a triangle morphism. Assume that for every object W of D, and for each i=1,2, the map Hom(U_i,W) -> colim over J opposite of Hom(H(j)_i,W), sending phi to the class of m_i followed by phi at j0, is bijective. Then for every W the corresponding map at i=3 is bijective. The triangle U and the morphism m are supplied data; no candidate value or denominator triangle is constructed in this statement.

source.place: Lemma 05SC proof, displayed five-term Hom diagram, dualized to contravariant Hom

proof.text: For each distinguished triangle, triangle_hom_exact proves the three exact pairs in the sequence Hom(second[1],W) -> Hom(first[1],W) -> Hom(third,W) -> Hom(second,W) -> Hom(first,W). Use Mathlib Triangle.yoneda_exact₂, yoneda_exact₃ and the two rotations; absorb the minus sign of the second rotation into the lifting morphism.

Construct homDiagram by the preadditive Yoneda functor followed by ULift to the universe max(uJ,vJ,vD), and take its actual abelian-group colimit. homColimMap_exact proves exactness by representing a kernel element, refining to a stage where its image is zero, and lifting using the pointwise exact pair. homColim_rep_eq_iff identifies equality in this group colimit with equality in the original ColimitType through the common-stage criterion; homComparison_bijective_iff transfers bijectivity.

The four natural transformations are the shifted first triangle arrow and the third, second and first arrows. homComparison_comm proves the corresponding four squares commute by colimit.ι_map and the triangle morphism equations; for the first square apply shiftFunctor.map to m.comm₁. homComparison_equivalence transports the first and second Hom comparisons across shiftEquiv D 1 using its adjunction Hom equivalence at W and its inverse image. This supplies the four outer bijections without any extra hypothesis.

Apply Mathlib AddMonoidHom.bijective_of_surjective_of_bijective_of_bijective_of_injective to these exact rows and commuting squares, using surjectivity of the first outer map, bijectivity of the second and fourth, and injectivity of the fifth. Transfer the resulting bijectivity of homComparison for the third component back to the stated ColimitType map.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05SC, displayed five-term Hom comparison, dualized; the element argument for exact filtered colimits is Tag 00DB, and the five lemma is Tag 05QB. Read from the Stacks tag pages because the local literature checkout is absent.

lean.statement:
theorem triangulated_hom_colimit_comparison
    {J : Type uJ} {D : Type uD} [Category.{vJ} J] [Category.{vD} D]
    [IsCofiltered J] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    (H : J ⥤ Triangle D) (hH : ∀ j, H.obj j ∈ distTriang D)
    (U : Triangle D) (hU : U ∈ distTriang D) (j₀ : J) (m : H.obj j₀ ⟶ U)
    (h₁ : ∀ W : D, Function.Bijective (fun φ : U.obj₁ ⟶ W ↦
      (((H ⋙ Triangle.π₁).op ⋙ yoneda.obj W).ιColimitType
        (Opposite.op j₀) (m.hom₁ ≫ φ))))
    (h₂ : ∀ W : D, Function.Bijective (fun φ : U.obj₂ ⟶ W ↦
      (((H ⋙ Triangle.π₂).op ⋙ yoneda.obj W).ιColimitType
        (Opposite.op j₀) (m.hom₂ ≫ φ)))) :
    ∀ W : D, Function.Bijective (fun φ : U.obj₃ ⟶ W ↦
      (((H ⋙ Triangle.π₃).op ⋙ yoneda.obj W).ιColimitType
        (Opposite.op j₀) (m.hom₃ ≫ φ)))
